title: OSHA construction excavations practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction excavations practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the section of 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P it comes from.

questions.question: Under Subpart P, a trench is an excavation whose width, measured at the bottom, is not greater than how much?
questions.explanation: A trench is a narrow excavation where "the width of a trench (measured at the bottom) is not greater than 15 feet (4.6 m)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.650, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Trench (Trench excavation) means a narrow excavation (in relation to its length) made below the surface of the ground. In general, the depth is greater than the width, but the width of a trench (measured at the bottom) is not greater than 15 feet (4.6 m).

questions.question: Besides being able to identify existing and predictable hazards, what must a competent person have under Subpart P?

options.C: A college degree in soil science
options.D: Authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate the hazards

questions.explanation: A competent person is one who can identify the hazards "and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.650, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Competent person means one who is capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings, or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.

questions.question: In a trench 4 feet or more deep, the means of egress must be located so employees travel no more than how far laterally?
questions.explanation: A safe means of egress must be located in such trenches "so as to require no more than 25 feet (7.62 m) of lateral travel for employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: so as to require no more than 25 feet (7.62 m) of lateral travel for employees

questions.question: A stairway, ladder, ramp or other safe means of egress is required in trench excavations of what depth?
questions.explanation: The rule requires safe means of egress "in trench excavations that are 4 feet (1.22 m) or more in depth."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall be located in trench excavations that are 4 feet (1.22 m) or more in depth

questions.question: If utility companies cannot respond to a locate request within how many hours (unless state or local law requires longer), may the employer proceed with caution using detection equipment?
questions.explanation: When utilities "cannot respond to a request to locate underground utility installations within 24 hours (unless a longer period is required by state or local law)," the employer may proceed with caution, using detection equipment or other acceptable means.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When utility companies or owners cannot respond to a request to locate underground utility installations within 24 hours (unless a longer period is required by state or local law), or cannot establish the exact location of these installations, the employer may proceed, provided the employer does so with caution, and provided detection equipment or other acceptable means to locate utility installations are used.

questions.topic: Water, adjacent structures and falling material
questions.question: What minimum distance from the edge does Subpart P set for keeping excavated materials and equipment, when retaining devices are not used?
questions.explanation: Protection is provided by "placing and keeping such materials or equipment at least 2 feet (.61 m) from the edge of excavations," or by retaining devices, or both.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Protection shall be provided by placing and keeping such materials or equipment at least 2 feet (.61 m) from the edge of excavations, or by the use of retaining devices that are sufficient to prevent materials or equipment from falling or rolling into excavations, or by a combination of both if necessary.

questions.question: Where a hazardous atmosphere could reasonably be expected, the atmosphere must be tested before employees enter excavations greater than what depth?
questions.explanation: In those conditions "the atmospheres in the excavation shall be tested before employees enter excavations greater than 4 feet (1.22 m) in depth."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: the atmospheres in the excavation shall be tested before employees enter excavations greater than 4 feet (1.22 m) in depth

questions.question: Subpart P describes oxygen deficiency as an atmosphere containing less than what percentage of oxygen?
questions.explanation: The rule refers to "oxygen deficiency (atmospheres containing less than 19.5 percent oxygen)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: oxygen deficiency (atmospheres containing less than 19.5 percent oxygen)

questions.question: Precautions such as ventilation must prevent exposure to a flammable gas concentration in excess of what share of the gas's lower flammable limit?
questions.explanation: Precautions must prevent exposure to "a concentration of a flammable gas in excess of 20 percent of the lower flammable limit of the gas."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: a concentration of a flammable gas in excess of 20 percent of the lower flammable limit of the gas

questions.question: An employee entering a bell-bottom pier hole wears a harness with a lifeline. What does Subpart P require of that lifeline?

options.A: It may double as the line used to handle materials
options.B: It needs attending only while the employee enters and exits
options.C: It must be separate from any material-handling line and individually attended at all times
options.D: It is needed only when the hole is deeper than 20 feet

questions.explanation: "The lifeline shall be separate from any line used to handle materials, and shall be individually attended at all times while the employee wearing the lifeline is in the excavation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The lifeline shall be separate from any line used to handle materials, and shall be individually attended at all times while the employee wearing the lifeline is in the excavation.

questions.topic: Water, adjacent structures and falling material
questions.question: When water removal equipment is used to control water in an excavation, who must monitor the equipment and operations?
questions.explanation: "The water removal equipment and operations shall be monitored by a competent person to ensure proper operation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: the water removal equipment and operations shall be monitored by a competent person to ensure proper operation

questions.question: When must the competent person inspect an excavation during a workday?

options.A: Only at the end of the shift
options.D: Prior to the start of work and as needed throughout the shift

questions.explanation: "An inspection shall be conducted by the competent person prior to the start of work and as needed throughout the shift," and also after every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing occurrence.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An inspection shall be conducted by the competent person prior to the start of work and as needed throughout the shift. Inspections shall also be made after every rainstorm or other hazard increasing occurrence.

questions.question: When the competent person finds evidence of a situation that could result in a possible cave-in, what does Subpart P require?

options.A: Employees keep working while the competent person watches the face
options.B: The employer files a report with OSHA within 24 hours
options.C: The employer posts a warning sign at the edge
options.D: Exposed employees are removed from the hazardous area until the necessary precautions have been taken

questions.explanation: In that case "exposed employees shall be removed from the hazardous area until the necessary precautions have been taken to ensure their safety."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: exposed employees shall be removed from the hazardous area until the necessary precautions have been taken to ensure their safety

questions.question: An excavation less than 5 feet deep (not in stable rock) can go without a protective system under what condition?

options.A: It will be open for less than 24 hours
options.B: Examination of the ground by a competent person provides no indication of a potential cave-in
options.D: Warning signs are posted at both ends

questions.explanation: The exception covers excavations "less than 5 feet (1.52m) in depth and examination of the ground by a competent person provides no indication of a potential cave-in."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Excavations are less than 5 feet (1.52m) in depth and examination of the ground by a competent person provides no indication of a potential cave-in.

questions.question: Under sloping Option (1), excavations may be sloped no steeper than which ratio?
questions.explanation: Option (1) says excavations "shall be sloped at an angle not steeper than one and one-half horizontal to one vertical (34 degrees measured from the horizontal)," unless another option is used.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Excavations shall be sloped at an angle not steeper than one and one-half horizontal to one vertical (34 degrees measured from the horizontal), unless the employer uses one of the other options listed below.

questions.question: Who must approve a sloping or benching system that does not use Option (1), (2) or (3)?
questions.explanation: Such systems "shall be approved by a registered professional engineer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Sloping and benching systems not utilizing Option (1) or Option (2) or Option (3) under paragraph (b) of this section shall be approved by a registered professional engineer.

questions.question: Where must the removal of a support system begin?

options.A: At the top of the excavation
options.B: At the bottom of the excavation
options.C: At the end nearest the spoil pile
options.D: At the middle of the trench

questions.explanation: "Removal shall begin at, and progress from, the bottom of the excavation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Removal shall begin at, and progress from, the bottom of the excavation.

questions.question: Employees are not allowed inside a shield while the shield is being what?

options.D: Used in a trench less than 8 feet deep

questions.explanation: "Employees shall not be allowed in shields when shields are being installed, removed, or moved vertically."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Employees shall not be allowed in shields when shields are being installed, removed, or moved vertically.

questions.topic: Soil classification and sloping (Appendices A and B)
questions.question: Under Appendix A, what must the classification of a soil or rock deposit be based on?

options.D: At least one visual and at least one manual analysis

questions.explanation: "The classification of the deposits shall be made based on the results of at least one visual and at least one manual analysis," done by a competent person.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR Part 1926, Subpart P, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The classification of the deposits shall be made based on the results of at least one visual and at least one manual analysis. Such analyses shall be conducted by a competent person

questions.topic: Soil classification and sloping (Appendices A and B)
questions.question: Under Appendix A, which of these is listed in the definition of Type C soil?

options.A: Cohesive soil with an unconfined compressive strength of 1.5 tsf or greater
options.B: Natural solid mineral matter that can be excavated with vertical sides and remain intact
options.C: Submerged soil or soil from which water is freely seeping
options.D: Cohesive soil with an unconfined compressive strength greater than 0.5 tsf but less than 1.5 tsf

questions.explanation: The definition of Type C lists "Submerged soil or soil from which water is freely seeping."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR Part 1926, Subpart P, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Submerged soil or soil from which water is freely seeping
